strings.tools.ffmpeg.name: FFmpeg Studio
strings.fields.input_file.label: Input Media File
strings.fields.output_dir.label: Output Folder
strings.actions.transcode.label: Transcode Media
strings.actions.fetch_ffmpeg.label: Download FFmpeg
strings.actions.fetch_ffprobe.label: Download FFprobe
strings.helpers.ffmpeg.name: ffmpeg
strings.helpers.ffmpeg.description: Required command-line engine for video/audio conversion, trimming, remuxing, and frame extraction.
strings.helpers.ffprobe.name: ffprobe
strings.helpers.ffprobe.description: Optional companion binary for fast JSON stream inspection (falls back to ffmpeg -i automatically).
strings.settings.video_preview.label: Video preview loading
strings.settings.video_preview.description: Control when the native video player opens after selecting a file. Switch to Trim & GIF Only or Manual for even faster Convert loading.
strings.settings.timeline_filmstrip.label: Timeline filmstrip thumbnails
strings.settings.timeline_filmstrip.description: Generate video frame thumbnails along the Trim & Merge and GIF & Frames timeline bar in the background. Turn off for instant loading.
strings.settings.preview_proxy.label: Non-native preview proxy
strings.settings.preview_proxy.description: How to preview formats the OS player cannot decode directly (MKV, WebM, AVI, VP9, AV1). Automatic builds proxies in the background; Fast Remux skips slow 480p transcodes.
strings.settings.hardware_accel.label: Hardware acceleration
strings.settings.hardware_accel.description: Use your OS GPU decoder and encoder (VideoToolbox, D3D11VA/NVENC, QSV, AMF, VA-API) for faster filmstrips, proxies, and exports with automatic CPU fallback.
strings.settings.hardware_backend.label: Hardware backend
strings.settings.hardware_backend.description: Choose which OS hardware acceleration backend FFmpeg Studio prefers when hardware acceleration is enabled.
